Expectation1: Attending children's school events and activities
Situation1: Children are about to finish school, and the father should pick them up
Expectation2: Listen actively and provide emotional support when needed.
Situation2: Your friend calls you in the middle of the night, crying, because they just received some devastating family news.
Story: It was nearly midnight when my phone buzzed. I saw my friend’s name flash on the screen, and when I answered, I could barely make out his words through his sobs. He’d just gotten terrible news about his father, and he needed someone to talk to—someone to listen, to be there. I sat on the edge of my bed, whispering comfort, trying to be the friend he needed. But as the minutes ticked by, I glanced at the clock and felt a knot tighten in my stomach. In just a few hours, I was supposed to be at my kids’ school, waiting at the gate to pick them up after their last big event of the year. They’d been talking about it for weeks, counting on me to be there. My friend’s pain was raw and immediate, but my children’s expectations were just as real. I felt torn, my heart pulled in two directions, wondering how I could possibly be the father and the friend I wanted to be, both at the same time.
